title: Thiacalix[4]arene-Supported Tetranuclear TbIII and EuIII Compounds: Synthesis, Structure, Luminescence, and Magnetism

synthesis.procedure: H4TC4A (0.15 g, 0.20 mmol), NaOH (0.008 g, 0.20 mmol), and Tb(acac)3·2H2O (0.40 g, 0.80 mmol) were added to toluene (4 mL). The mixture was refluxed at 110 °C for 24 h. After filtration, the residue was dissolved in CH2Cl2/CH3OH (1:1 v/v) and allowed to stand at room temperature for 5 d to give colorless crystals of 1. Crystals were heated at 40 °C under vacuum for 0.5 h to obtain desolvated samples.

properties.summary: Solid-state green TbIII luminescence at room temperature (excitation 335 nm) with characteristic 5D4→7FJ bands, strongest at 546 nm. DC magnetism of 1 shows χMT = 48.27 cm3·K·mol−1 at 300 K falling to 22.33 cm3·K·mol−1 at 2 K, Curie–Weiss C = 48.90 cm3·K·mol−1 and θ = −0.53 K indicating antiferromagnetic Tb···Tb coupling; M = 20.55 Nβ at 2 K/70 kOe without saturation and no hysteresis at 2 K. AC susceptibility under 2 Oe (11–999 Hz) shows no χ″ peaks or frequency dependence at 0 or 1 kOe dc field down to 2 K.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to 1 except Eu(acac)3·2H2O was used instead of Tb(acac)3·2H2O: H4TC4A (0.15 g, 0.20 mmol), NaOH (0.008 g, 0.20 mmol), and Eu(acac)3·2H2O in toluene (4 mL) were refluxed at 110 °C for 24 h; the residue was recrystallized from CH2Cl2/CH3OH (1:1 v/v) at room temperature over 5 d to give colorless block crystals. Crystals were heated at 40 °C under vacuum for 0.5 h to obtain desolvated samples.
